findings.headline: Smaller premiums elsewhere on the schedule.
findings.body: Your overdraft fee ($35 vs a $32 median, n=15) and your incoming wire fee ($25 vs a $14.50 median, n=16) also sit above the peer 75th percentile. Individually modest, together they shape how the schedule reads in a side-by-side comparison.

exec_narrative: HomeTrust Bank is compared with 68 banks of similar size nationwide that publish fee schedules in the Bank Fee Index; a national set is used because fewer than 15 same-size peers in North Carolina have published data, so local competitors may price differently. Of 9 rankable lines, five sit inside the middle half of the market, three above it (NSF / returned-item fee, overdraft fee and incoming wire fee), and one below it (paper statement fee). We would suggest one step: review the NSF / returned-item fee, which sits above the market range; the peer median of $32 is the reference point.

callouts.title: NSF / returned-item fee — $35
callouts.stat: Peer median $32 · middle half $31.50–$33.50 · range $30–$37 · 92nd percentile · n=12
callouts.body: Published as “Returned Item charge.” At $35 it is $3 above the $32 peer median. Returned-item fees remain under regulatory and competitive pressure, and a number of large institutions have eliminated them. A penalty fee offers little service to differentiate on, so the peer median of $32 is the natural reference point.

callouts.title: Overdraft fee — $35
callouts.stat: Peer median $32 · middle half $30–$33.50 · range $10–$36 · 93rd percentile · n=15
callouts.body: Published as “Overdraft charge.” At $35 it is $3 above the $32 peer median. Overdraft pricing is the first line examiners, consumer advocates and comparison sites read. A penalty fee offers little service to differentiate on, so the peer median of $32 is the natural reference point.

callouts.title: Incoming wire fee — $25
callouts.stat: Peer median $14.50 · middle half $10–$15 · range $10–$20 · 100th percentile · n=16
callouts.body: Published as “Wire transfer - incoming domestic U.S. dollar.” At $25 it is $10.50 above the $14.50 peer median. Charging to receive funds is increasingly uncommon and is noticed by business customers. Holding the premium is reasonable if the service behind it is differentiated; otherwise the peer median of $14.50 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Paper statement fee — $1.50
callouts.stat: Peer median $3 · middle half $2–$3 · 0th percentile · n=11
callouts.body: Published as “Mailed paper statement fee.” A customer-favorable price on a low-volume line. No action is indicated unless it is an old price that was never revisited, in which case the peer median of $3 is the reference point.

context_narrative:
Overdraft and returned-item fees have been the focus of regulatory and public attention since 2022, and many of the largest banks have reduced overdraft fees or eliminated NSF fees outright. Community institutions have moved more slowly and more unevenly, which is why the spread inside a peer set is often wider than the headline national averages suggest.

Fee schedules are also now public in a practical sense: they are collected, compared and summarized automatically. A customer or examiner comparing HomeTrust Bank with its peers sees the same published lines this report uses, so the schedule is a positioning document as much as a pricing one.

How to use this report: § 02 shows every line against the peer range; § 03 explains the lines that sit outside it; § 05 names peers line by line. Ranked comparisons require at least eight peers publishing the same line. Where your institution offers several amounts for one category, the report uses the standard consumer charge described in the methodology below.
